summary: The core product, ATT&CK-mapped Windows logging configs, is already given away: sysmon-modular is MIT-licensed and maintained, Yamato Security maps audit settings to Sigma coverage, Sentinel ships curated event sets, and Cribl is free to 1TB/day. MSP-focused SIEMs (Huntress, Blumira, LimaCharlie) remove the volume pain. What's left to sell is a thin maintenance and reporting layer.

objections.objection: Free, maintained, ATT&CK-mapped configs already exist and are what MSSPs reach for first. Olaf Hartong's sysmon-modular (MIT, 3.2k stars, active CI, ATT&CK Navigator export, balanced/verbose/MDE-augment profiles) and Yamato Security's EnableWindowsLogSettings (audit settings with per-log Sigma rule counts) cover the open-source baseline and much of the 'detection-mapped, maintained' paid claim. The concept's table lumps these together as generic 'community configs', but they are neither generic nor unmaintained.

Platform bundling already does the volume-reduction job inside the SIEMs the concept targets. Microsoft Sentinel's Windows Security Events connector offers curated Minimal and Common event sets, which Microsoft describes as reducing volume while keeping a full audit trail, plus XPath/DCR filtering at no extra charge. Microsoft also now ships built-in Sysmon and could publish a recommended config at any time. The Sentinel slice of the market therefore gets most of the 'log diet' free from the vendor.

Cribl Stream is free up to 1TB/day with no licence, which covers every MSSP in the stated 10-150 SMB-client range. Its Pack Dispensary has shipped Windows event reduction packs claiming 25-70% reduction. The concept compares itself only to Cribl's paid Standard tier and says 'we need no pipeline'. An MSSP with any engineering capacity can get the same reduction free, with a community behind it.

The MSP channel is moving to flat-priced or per-sensor managed SIEMs that do the filtering themselves. Huntress Managed SIEM applies Smart Filtering at the source and prices per data source with a SOC included. Blumira is flat per employee. LimaCharlie charges about $3 per sensor including Windows event logs and offers MSSP tiers. On these platforms the volume ROI behind the $249/month disappears. The concept admits this risk but its competitor table understates it: Huntress is the most dangerous competitor because it already owns the MSP relationship.

Commercial detection-content vendors sell adjacent coverage-gap products to MSSPs. SOC Prime's Data Audit maps SIEM data to ATT&CK to find blind spots and is sold alongside thousands of Sigma rules with MSSP/MDR tiers. It could add 'collect these events, drop those' recommendations as a feature. Graylog Illuminate and Wazuh's default Windows/Sysmon rulesets could likewise ship tuned collection guidance.

The logon evidence pack competes with cheap, entrenched tools. ManageEngine ADAudit Plus starts at about $245/year (100 workstations) and $495/year (2 file servers), per the input's own flagged claim, and has turnkey reports. SIEM-native report queries are a weaker substitute for MSPs who just want a PDF for the client.

strongest_point: No vendor sells one SIEM-agnostic, monthly-maintained Windows collection layer that covers Wazuh, Graylog, Elastic and Sentinel and is deployed through MSP RMM tools. That niche is real, if narrow.
what_would_change_my_mind: Interviews with 10 small MSSPs on volume-billed SIEMs showing that at least 5 tried sysmon-modular, Sentinel event sets or free Cribl and still pay to close the gap
Pilot data showing QuietWin packs cut 30%+ more volume than sysmon-modular plus Sentinel 'Common' at equal Sigma coverage
An RMM or SIEM vendor (NinjaOne, Graylog, Wazuh) agreeing to OEM or resell the packs
